drafts.draft_en:
Hey @grok, a Philly homeowner owns a rowhome with a small mortgage left, and it needs major repairs.

She has to choose:
A) Sell as-is to a cash buyer this month
B) Borrow for the repairs and list it in 6 months

Compare both: net proceeds, carrying costs, timeline, and what can go wrong.
drafts.pattern: A/B choice ask with family/mortgage stakes (@0_3_BTC, 25.7k in ~19h). Localized to a Philly distressed seller. Hypothetical scenario; no numbers promised, let Grok run them and you correct.
drafts.video_tip: 12s in front of a rowhome needing work: hold up two fingers, 'Option A or option B?', read both. End: 'Let's see what Grok says, then I'll tell you what I'd actually do after 25+ years of these deals.' Burned-in captions; quote-post Grok's answer.

drafts.draft_en:
Hey @grok, if you were 30, renting in Philadelphia, with $25K saved and a $70K salary, map out the exact playbook to buy a 2-unit property in the next 24 months and house hack it.

Month by month. Real numbers only.

drafts.video_tip: Phone-screen recording: type the question into X, post it, cut to Grok's reply. Overlay: 'Grok's plan vs. what actually works in Philly' and stitch your 30s reaction with one correction.

Hey @grok, if prices keep rising at today's pace, what will a typical Philadelphia rowhome cost, and what will average rent be, when my newborn turns 30?

Real numbers only.
